headline.title: First flakes for Northern Vermont.
headline.text: Up to {{s:1.8}} on the summit of Jay Peak this week. 2 of the 31 resorts close to opening get nights cold enough to make snow, mostly in Western Maine. Killington typically opens first, around Nov 8.

BTV.excerpt:
Scattered rain showers will impact the region on Thursday, with rainfall amounts ranging between a few hundredths to a few tenths of an inch.
Unsettled weather with temperatures slowly returning closer to normal expected on Saturday. 3. Drier early next week with showers later in the week.

ALY.excerpt:
) After a dry and unseasonably warm day today, a weak cold front will bring beneficial rain showers tomorrow. Additional chances of rain continue into Friday, primarily south and east of the Capital District.
) A disturbance on Saturday will increase rain chances for eastern New York and western New England, with temperatures trending back towards normal into early next week.

GYX.excerpt:
Warming peaks today with temperatures challenging records.
A widespread soaking rainfall is possible for the late week into the weekend along a slow moving frontal boundary.

PHI.excerpt: ) A slow moving cold front approaches and moves through the area on Friday, bringing the potential for heavy rain to portions of the area beginning on Thursday.

CTP.excerpt:
) Unseasonably mild through Friday with 2.5 weeks-long dry spell coming to an end overnight into Thursday
) Trending cooler this weekend with lake enhanced rain showers beneath upper level low

RLX.excerpt:
) A cold front brings showers and possibly a few thunderstorms today into Thursday.
) Much cooler temperatures arrive this weekend behind the cold front setting up frost/freeze concerns across our active growing season counties.

writeups.name: Vermont
writeups.title: Quiet and mild.
paras: Next two days: summit temperatures from {{t:46}} to {{t:65}}, with rain at times.
Killington usually opens first here, around Nov 8. Nights stay too mild to make much snow this week.
NWS Burlington forecasters, Wednesday 2:31 PM: "Scattered rain showers will impact the region on Thursday, with rainfall amounts ranging between a few hundredths to a few tenths of an inch."
writeups.outlook: Days 8 to 14: NOAA's outlook leans slightly warmer than normal and slightly drier than normal.

writeups.title: Just a coating for the high peaks.
paras: Light snow Saturday evening to early Sunday: Whiteface {{s:0.5}} at the summits, though the models range from {{r:0,3.1}} at Whiteface. Rain mixes in at the bases.
Next two days: summit temperatures from {{t:42}} to {{t:71}}, with rain at times.
